page.title: What Is a Variable in Python?
page.introduction: Before working with functions, classes, data structures, and other Python concepts, it is important to understand how Python associates names with objects.
page.definition: A variable in Python is a name that refers to an object stored in memory.

explanation.content: When Python executes x = 10, the name x becomes associated with an integer object representing the value 10.
A Python variable is therefore better understood as a name binding or reference rather than a box that directly contains a value.
The visual model below shows the basic relationship between a variable name and the object to which that name refers.

visual.introduction: Think of a Python variable as a name that provides a way to reach and work with an object.

explanation.content: In x = 10, Python creates or uses an integer object representing 10 and binds the name x to that object.
The name x is not the object itself. It is a reference that allows the program to access the object.

page.takeaway: A Python variable is best understood as a name bound to an object. This name–object relationship is fundamental to understanding assignment, object identity, mutability, and function arguments.
